answer: A voyage-based reputation bond resists sybils: before an agent can bid, it must stake a refundable deposit that unlocks only after completing verified work over time, like a ship earning trust across many ports. Attackers face real cost per identity: each fake must fund its own bond and wait out the voyage, while honest agents reuse one bond. A gale of cheap clones therefore stalls at the deposit gate, and a nebula of fake reviews cannot outvote staked, time-tested identities because voting weight follows completed work, not account count.
